data.headline: Overnight funding eases as Treasury yields rise
data.summary: SOFR was 3.88% on November 9, down from 3.89% on November 6. In the latest Treasury observations, dated November 6, the two-year yield rose 5 basis points to 4.51% and the ten-year rose 2 to 4.86%. The spread narrowed to 35 basis points.

bull.text: November 9 SOFR was 1 basis point lower than November 6. Borrowers whose rates reset against SOFR can see some relief when credit spreads and contract terms are unchanged.

bear.text: From November 5 to 6, the two-year yield rose from 4.46% to 4.51% and the ten-year from 4.84% to 4.86%. The ten-year minus two-year spread narrowed from 38 to 35 basis points.

watch.text: From October 27 to November 3, the net short held by leveraged funds in E-mini S&P 500 futures narrowed by 28,286 contracts to 372,318. Their net short in E-mini Russell 2000 futures widened by 6,999 contracts to 55,080.

limitations: Overnight funding and Treasury yields have different observation dates. This brief contains no November 10 price or economic release observations.
The CFTC observations are weekly futures positions as of November 3. ETF flows and investor intent require separate evidence.
